Consider the graph of the function $f(x),$ shown above. It consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the line segment for $x\in [0,4]$ and the line segment for $x\in [4,6].$ Therefore, we can write the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{4}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}
$$

The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,4].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+1)\cdot 4 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [4,6].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(5+1)\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =10+6 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
